newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil- Prices seen softer on better weather.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil- Prices seen softer on better weather.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to soften this week on prospects of better weather conditions in the southern Mindanao island, Manila vegetable oil traders said on Monday.
"I expect prices to either remain unchanged or slip this week due to improving copra harvests in the country," said one senior Manila vegetable oil trader.
The Philippines is the world's largest exporter of coconut oil.

Philippine coconut oil exports in the first two months of the year increased to 142,200 tonnes from the year-ago 137,699 tonnes, trade group United Coconut Association of the Philippines (UCAP) said on Monday.
UCAP said the figures were preliminary.
UCAP also said preliminary data showed coconut oil exports for February alone was at 57,200 tonnes compared to 63,625 tonnes in February 1996.

Traders attributed the drop in the export figures last month due to rains in the southern Mindanao island. "The rains delayed copra deliveries to the mills," a senior vegetable oil trader in Manila said
Mindanao accounts for 55 percent of Philippine coconut output and 80 percent of the country's coconut oil exports, a trader at a U.S.-based commodity house said.

Traders said they expected production to pick-up in Mindanao this month due to prospects of an improving weather situation. "Copra is coming out again. Henceforth we see increasing exports from Manila," the trader added.
Coconut oil stocks in Rotterdam also remain high, traders said.
Stocks of the commodity in Rotterdam dipped to 19,263 tonnes as of February 24 from 24,625 tonnes as of February 18.
